STUDYQURAN:16:78/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:78/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:78/r1.claim: As God brings milk from cattle, honey from bees, and the Hour from the unseen, He also brings humans from their mothers’ wombs.
STUDYQURAN:16:78/r1.anchor: Just as God brings things forth from hidden places—milk from the bellies of cattle (v. 66), honey from the bellies of bees (v. 69), and the Hour from the realm of the Unseen (v. 77)—so does He bring forth human beings

STUDYQURAN:16:78/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:78/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:78/r2.claim: People are born knowing nothing; together with 16:70 and 30:54, this shows that strength and knowledge wax and wane through life.
STUDYQURAN:16:78/r2.anchor: Human beings are born knowing naught; see v. 70 and 30:54, which together indicate that human beings’ strength and knowledge wax and wane throughout the course of their lives.

STUDYQURAN:16:78/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:78/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:78/r3.claim: Hearing, sight, and hearts are repeatedly grouped as divine gifts.
STUDYQURAN:16:78/r3.anchor: Hearing, sight, and hearts are repeatedly mentioned all together or in various combinations as Divine gifts (10:31; 23:78; 32:9).

STUDYQURAN:16:78/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:78/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:78/r4.claim: These faculties enable people to receive guidance and acquire religious knowledge and understanding.
STUDYQURAN:16:78/r4.anchor: These are the faculties through which guidance is received and through which religious knowledge and understanding are acquired (22:46)

STUDYQURAN:16:78/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:78/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:78/r5.claim: Some people’s faculties become corrupted and impervious to divine guidance.
STUDYQURAN:16:78/r5.anchor: but the Quran states that these faculties are corrupted in some human beings, so that they become impervious to Divine Guidance

TAB-FULL:v14p315/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p315/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p315/r1.claim: After birth, God teaches people what they did not know and gives them reason to understand and distinguish good from evil; He enables them to see and hear after they had known nothing.
TAB-FULL:v14p315/r1.anchor: والله أخرجكم من بطون أمهاتكم لا تعلمون شيئا

TAB-FULL:v14p315/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p315/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p315/r2.claim: Hearing receives sounds and lets people understand one another's conversation; sight sees people, allowing recognition and distinction between them.
TAB-FULL:v14p315/r2.anchor: السمع الذي تسمعون به الأصوات، فيفقه بعضكم عن بعض ما تتحاورون به بينكم، والأبصار التي تبصرون بها الأشخاص

TAB-FULL:v14p315/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p315/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p315/r3.claim: The afʾidah are hearts by which people know and retain things, reflect on them, and understand them.
TAB-FULL:v14p315/r3.anchor: يقول: والقلوب التي تعرفون بها الأشياء فتحفظونها

TAB-FULL:v14p315/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p315/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p315/r4.claim: God bestowed these faculties so people would thank Him alone, not idols or partners that had no share in His blessings; the phrase is cited also at 2:52.
TAB-FULL:v14p315/r4.anchor: فعلنا ذلك بكم، فاشكروا الله على ما أنعم به عليكم من ذلك، دون الآلهة والأنداد

TAB-FULL:v14p315/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p315/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p315/r5.claim: The birth clause is a complete statement, followed by a new clause about the faculties; physical faculties were given before birth, but knowledge and reason after birth.
TAB-FULL:v14p315/r5.anchor: كلام متناه، ثم ابتدئ الخبر، فقيل: وجعل الله لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة وإنما قلنا ذلك كذلك

TABATABAI:16:78-79/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r1.claim: The passage moves from further divine favors to proofs of God's oneness in lordship, resurrection, prophecy, and legislation, paralleling the preceding group of verses.
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r1.anchor: تذكر عدة أخرى من النعم الإلهية ثم تعطف الكلام إلى ما تكشف عنه من حق القول في وحدانيته تعالى

TABATABAI:16:78-79/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r2.claim: أمهات is a plural of أم with an added feminine ه, analogous to إهراق from أراق; أمات is also used.
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r2.anchor: الأمهات جمع أم والهاء زائدة نظير إهراق وأصله أراق وقد تأتي أمات

TABATABAI:16:78-79/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r3.claim: One reported usage distinguishes أمهات for human mothers from أمات for mothers of other animals.
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r3.anchor: وقيل الأمهات في الإنسان والأمات في غيره من الحيوان

TABATABAI:16:78-79/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r4.claim: أفئدة is a broken plural of paucity for فؤاد, meaning heart or core; no plural of abundance is attested for it.
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r4.anchor: والأفئدة جمع قلة للفؤاد وهو القلب

TABATABAI:16:78-79/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r5.claim: At birth, people lack acquired sensory, imaginative, and intellectual knowledge; this supports the view that the mind is initially blank, while self-awareness is not included.
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r5.anchor: والحال أن نفوسكم خالية من هذه المعلومات التي أحرزتموها من طريق الحس والخيال والعقل بعد ذلك

TABATABAI:16:78-79/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r6.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r6.claim: Some argue the verse also denies immediate self-knowledge at first; al-Tabatabai rejects this, taking its scope as acquired knowledge, as the old-age verse confirms.
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r6.anchor: واحتج بعضهم بعموم الآية على أن العلم الحضوري يعني به علم الإنسان بنفسه كسائر العلوم الحصولية

TABATABAI:16:78-79/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r7.claim: Senses are the starting point of conception, especially hearing and sight alongside touch, taste, and smell; the heart is the source of thought.
TABATABAI:16:78-79/r7.anchor: والعمدة فيه السمع والبصر وإن كان هناك غيرهما

TABRISI:16:78-80/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:78-80/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:78-80/r6.claim: The original form of أمهات is أمات; the ه was added for emphasis, as in أهرقت, whose original form is أرقت.
TABRISI:16:78-80/r6.anchor: الأمهات أصله الأمات ولكن الهاء زيدت مؤكدة

TABRISI:16:78-80/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:78-80/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:78-80/r7.claim: أفئدة is the plural of فؤاد, like أغربة from غراب; it has no plural فئدان on the pattern used for غربان.
TABRISI:16:78-80/r7.anchor: والأفئدة جمع فؤاد كما يقال غراب وأغربة

TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r2.claim: The phrase لا تعلمون شيئا is a circumstantial clause attached to the second-person pronoun; شيئا can be a cognate accusative meaning no knowledge, or an object if تعلمون means تعرفون.
TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r2.anchor: في موضع نصب على الحال من الكاف والميم

TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r3.claim: شيئا may be parsed as an accusative cognate object for لا تعلمون علما, or as the object of تعلمون understood as تعرفون.
TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مفعولا ويكون تعلمون بمعنى تعرفون

TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r5.claim: God brought people from their mothers' wombs while they knew none of their benefits or harms, then gave them sound senses as routes to knowledge and hearts as the seat of understanding so they would thank Him.

TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r6.claim: Hearing and sight are sound faculties that lead to knowledge of perceptions; hearts are the place of knowledge by which people understand things.
TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r6.anchor: بالحواس الصحيحة التي هي طرق إلى العلم بالمدركات وتفضل عليكم بالقلوب التي تفقهون بها الأشياء

TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r7.claim: The purpose is that people thank and praise God for these gifts.
TABRISI:16:78-80#2/r7.anchor: أي لكي تشكروه على ذلك وتحمدوه

THALABI:v6p32/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p32/r11.speaker: الأعمش
THALABI:v6p32/r11.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads the word with kasra on both the alif and mīm.
THALABI:v6p32/r11.anchor: قرأ الأعمش: إمهاتكم بكسر الألف والميم

THALABI:v6p32/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p32/r12.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
THALABI:v6p32/r12.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read with kasra on the alif and fatḥa on the mīm.
THALABI:v6p32/r12.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بكسر الألف وفتح الميم

THALABI:v6p32/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p32/r13.speaker: الباقون
THALABI:v6p32/r13.claim: The remaining readers use fatḥa on the mīm and ḍamma on the alif.
THALABI:v6p32/r13.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بضم الألف وفتح الميم

THALABI:v6p32/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p32/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p32/r14.claim: The original form is ummāt; hāʾ was added for emphasis, like ahraqt from araqt.
THALABI:v6p32/r14.anchor: وأصل الأمهات: أمات، فزيدت الهاء للتأكيد

THALABI:v6p32/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p32/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p32/r15.claim: The clause saying you knew nothing is complete; the next clause begins a new sentence.
THALABI:v6p32/r15.anchor: لا تعلمون شيئا هذا كلام تام. ثم ابتدأ فقال: وجعل لكم السمع

THALABI:v6p32/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p32/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p32/r16.claim: God created these faculties before birth but bestowed knowledge after birth so people would give thanks for His blessings.
THALABI:v6p32/r16.anchor: لأن الله تعالى جعل [لعباده السمع] والأبصار والأفئدة قبل إخراجهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r1.claim: Being born knowing nothing means being brought into the world ignorant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {والله أخرجكم من بطون أمهاتكم لا تعلمون شيئا} أي أخرجكم غير عالمين بمعنى: أخرجكم جاهلين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r2.claim: The creation of hearing, sight, and hearts is coordinated with bringing people out; the order of mention does not imply that these faculties were created later, since waw does not impose sequence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة} عطف (¬3) على قوله: {أخرجكم}، وجعل السمع كان قبل الإخراج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r3.claim: God created the senses through which people learn and discover what they did not know.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r3.anchor: والمعنى: خلق لكم الحواس التي بها تعلمون وتقفون على ما تجهلون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the faculties let people hear God’s admonitions, see His blessings from birth to adulthood, and understand His greatness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس في هذه الآية: يريد لتسمعوا مواعظ الله وتبصروا ما أنعم الله به عليكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r5.claim: Afʾida is the plural of fuʾād, following the pattern of ghurāb and aghriba.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj notes that fuʾād lacks the larger plural form fiʾdān, unlike ghurāb, which has ghurbān.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p152/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج: ولم يجمع فؤاد على أكثر العدد؛ لم يقل فيه: فئدان، كما قيل في غراب وغربان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:76-78/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:76-78/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:76-78/r11.claim: God created the faculties by which people learn and come to know what was unknown to them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:76-78/r11.anchor: خلق لكم الحواس التي بها يعلمون، ويقفون على ما يجهلون

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p78/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p78/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p78/r6.claim: God gave people hearing, sight, and hearts so they would give thanks.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p78/r6.anchor: وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة لعلكم تشكرون} [النحل: 78] لكي تشكروا.

ELMALILI:16:77-79/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:16:77-79/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:16:77-79/r1.claim: Elmalılı sees this verse as supporting empiricism and the training or practice school in theories of knowledge.
ELMALILI:16:77-79/r1.anchor: Bu âyet ilim nazariyesinde ihtibar ve tedrib mezhebini müeyyid görünüyor.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r1.claim: The singular fu'ad is generally explained as heart; in older sources, in contexts about knowing, heart also means the power of understanding or intellect, alongside the Turkish sense of inner feeling.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r1.anchor: kalp ise Türkçe’deki “gönül” mânasının yanında, özellikle eski kaynaklarda, bilgi olayıyla ilgili olduğu konumlarda “bilme ve kavrama gücü, akıl” anlamında kullanılmaktadır (Râgıb el-İsfahânî

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r2.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r2.claim: Tabari glosses ef'idah as intellects: God taught people after birth, giving them the mental capacity to acquire knowledge, distinguish good from bad, recognize and retain things, and reason deeply.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r3.claim: In Tabari's explanation, fu'ad, heart, and intellect are interchangeable as terms for the cognitive faculty, a point the authors consider important for Qur'anic semantics.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r3.anchor: bu açıklamada fuâd, kalp ve akıl terimleri, “bilgi melekesi” mânasında eş anlamlı olarak kullanılmış olup Taberî’nin bu ifadeleri Kur’an semantiği bakımından son derece önemlidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r4.claim: Emphasizing that people know nothing at birth and are given hearing, sight, and intellect highlights knowledge and thought as their most valuable capacity and calls for gratitude.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r4.anchor: insanın en değerli özelliğinin bilgi ve düşünme kapasitesi olduğuna ve nimete şükretmek gerektiğine işaret etmesi bakımından anlamlıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r5.claim: Mentioning these faculties here is meant to prompt reflection on the subjects in the following verses and to draw lessons that guide toward good.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:78/r5.anchor: muhatabın bundan sonraki âyetlerde ele alınan konular üzerinde düşünüp bunlardan hidayet ve hayra yöneltici dersler çıkarmasını sağlamak

QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r1.claim: God conceals the unseen and people's ends: He may lead people from error or hostility into sainthood, so no one knows the destiny prepared for them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r1.anchor: فالعواقب مستورة ، والخواتيم مبهمة ، والخلق في غفلة عما يراد بهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r2.claim: People were created without consultation or choice, and at birth they did not know whether their lot was happiness or misery, their own welfare, or their Lord.
QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r2.anchor: خلقهم من غير أن شاورهم ، وأثبتهم - على الوصف الذي أراده - دون أن خيرهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r3.claim: By divine inspiration, even an infant is guided to take its mother's breast without prior instruction, warning, command, or rebuke.
QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r3.anchor: ثم بحكم الإلهام هداهم حتى قبل الصبي ثدي أمه وإن لم يكن قد تقدمه تعريف

QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r4.claim: Hearing is given to hear God's address, sight to behold His acts, and hearts to know His right.
QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r4.anchor: جعل لكم السمع } : لتسمعوا خطابه ، { والأبصار } لتبصروا أفعاله ، { والأفئدة } لتعرفوا حقه

QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r5.claim: These senses are gifts meant to lead people to gratitude for God's immense beneficence.
QUSHAYRI:v2p165/r5.anchor: ثم لتشكروا عظيم إنعامه عليكم بهذه الحواس

BURHAN:v3p239#4/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p239#4/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p239#4/r11.claim: Darkness precedes light in perception, and ignorance precedes spiritual understanding; being born without knowledge illustrates this precedence.
BURHAN:v3p239#4/r11.anchor: فإن الظلمات سابقة على النور في الإحساس وكذلك الظلمة المعنوية سابقة على النور المعنوي

BURHAN:v4p149/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p149/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p149/r4.claim: ألم يروا إلى الطير lacks a conjunction because it links by inference to God bringing people from their mothers’ wombs.
BURHAN:v4p149/r4.anchor: ولا ينتقض هذا الاصل بقوله في النحل ﴿ ألم يروا إلى الطير ﴾ 5 لاتصالها بقوله ﴿ والله أخرجكم من بطون أمهاتكم ﴾ 6

BURHAN:v4p154/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p154/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p154/r5.claim: Cognitive علم takes meanings as its object, as in لا تعلمون شيئا.
BURHAN:v4p154/r5.anchor: علم العرفانية لا تتعلق إلا بالمعاني نحو ﴿ لا تعلمون شيئا ﴾

SULAMI:v1p370#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p370#3/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p370#3/r1.claim: Newborns know nothing of the primordial covenant taken from them at the time of 'Am I not your Lord?'.
SULAMI:v1p370#3/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي : أخرجكم من بطون أمهاتكم لا تفهمون شيئا مما أخذت عليكم من الميثاق في وقت بلى .

SULAMI:v1p370#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p370#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p370#3/r2.claim: At birth people know nothing of their decreed felicity or misery; God gives the successful hearing for subtle remembrance, sight for His signs, and hearts for knowing their Maker, making the faculties a cause for gratitude.
SULAMI:v1p370#3/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لا تعلمون شيئا مما قضيت لكم وعليكم من الشقاوة والسعادة . ثم جعل للسعيد من عباده السمع

SULAMI:v1p370#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p370#3/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان المغربي
SULAMI:v1p370#3/r3.claim: Hearing receives the commands and prohibitions, sight witnesses the wonders of divine power, and hearts recognize the traces of truth's gifts.
SULAMI:v1p370#3/r3.anchor: قال أبو عثمان المغربي : جعل لكم السمع لتسمعوا به خطاب الأمر والنهي ، والأبصار لتبصروا بها عجائب القدرة ،

SULAMI:v1p371/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p371/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p371/r1.claim: Giving thanks means recognizing God's continuing gifts and returning to Him.
SULAMI:v1p371/r1.anchor: أي لعلكم تبصرون دوام نعمي عليكم فترجعوا إلى بابي .

SULAMI:v1p371/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p371/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p371/r2.claim: The completion of blessing is being granted contentment with the courses of divine decree.
SULAMI:v1p371/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : تمام النعمة هو أن يرزق العبد الرضا بمجاري القضاء .

SULAMI:v1p371/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p371/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p371/r3.claim: The completion of blessing is gnosis in this world and vision of God in the next.
SULAMI:v1p371/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : تمام النعمة في الدنيا المعرفة وفي الآخرة الرؤية .

SULAMI:v1p371/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p371/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p371/r4.claim: Complete blessing is delight in surrender and relinquishing self-direction.
SULAMI:v1p371/r4.anchor: وسئل بعضهم : ما تمام النعمة ؟ قال : هو التنعم في الاستسلام وإسقاط التدبير .

SULAMI:v1p371/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p371/r5.speaker: أبو محمد الجريري
SULAMI:v1p371/r5.claim: Complete blessing is a heart free of hidden associating and a self free of ostentation and desire for reputation.
SULAMI:v1p371/r5.anchor: قال أبو محمد الجريري : تمام النعمة خلو القلب من الشرك الخفي وسلامة النفس من الرياء والسمعة .

NAHHAS:v2p404/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p404/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p404/r6.claim: Some readers break the hamza by vowel harmony; kasra on the mīm is unlikely. أمّهات is the plural of أمّهة, though others call its hā augmentative as in أهرقت.
NAHHAS:v2p404/r6.anchor: وكسر الميم بعيد وأمهات جمع أمهة

SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r1.claim: لا تعلمون شيئا is a circumstantial clause describing the people when brought out: you were brought out without knowledge.
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r1.anchor: الجملة حال من مفعول " أخرجكم " ، أي: أخرجكم غير عالمين.

SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r2.claim: شيئا may be an object, or a verbal noun meaning 'any knowledge'; العلم here means knowing or recognizing.
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r2.anchor: و " شيئا " إما مصدر، أي: شيئا من العلم، وإما مفعول به. والعلم هنا العرفان.

SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r3.claim: The author notes that he discussed أمهاتكم earlier in the chapter of al-Nisaʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r3.anchor: وقد تقدم الكلام في " أمهاتكم " في النساء.

SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r4.claim: وجعل may coordinate with أخرجكم, remaining within the report about God, or begin a new sentence.
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r4.anchor: قوله: " وجعل " يجوز أن يكون معطوفا على " أخرجكم " فيكون داخلا فيما أخبر به عن المبتدأ، ويجوز أن يكون مستأنفا.

SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r5.claim: الأفئدة is the plural of فؤاد.

SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r6.speaker: الرازي
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r6.claim: Al-Razi says the plural is a form of paucity because most people are occupied with bestial acts, as though they had no heart.
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r6.anchor: وقال الرازي: " إنما جمع جمع قلة؛ لأن أكثر الناس مشغولون بأفعال بهيمية فكأنهم لا فؤاد لهم ".

SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says forms such as أفئدة are used for both few and many although only a paucity form is attested; he compares شسوع.
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r7.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " إنه من الجموع التي استعملت للقلة والكثرة، ولم يسمع فيها غير القلة، نحو: " شسوع "

SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r8.claim: The author questions al-Zamakhshari's claim that only شسوع is heard, since أشساع is also attested; he says شسوع should be called predominant.
SAMIN-DURR:16:78/r8.anchor: كذا قال، وفيه نظر. سمع منهم " أشساع " فكان ينبغي أن يقول: غلب شسوع.

ZAJJAJ:v3p214/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p214/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p214/r4.claim: The form immahātikum is vocalized with kasra; the original plural is amāt, with hā added for emphasis, as in ahrāqtu from araqtu.

ZAJJAJ:v3p214/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p214/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p214/r5.claim: Afʾida is the plural of fuʾād, like aghriba is the plural of غراب.
ZAJJAJ:v3p214/r5.anchor: والأفئدة جمع فؤاد مثل غراب وأغربة

ZAJJAJ:v3p214/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p214/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p214/r6.claim: Fuʾād is not given a further plural of the larger-count pattern; one does not say fuʾdān, just as the pattern is not used for غراب.
ZAJJAJ:v3p214/r6.anchor: ولم يجمع فؤاد على أكثر العدد، لم يقل فئدان

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7/r1.claim: The Qur'an's small verbal differences are intentional in every detail and display the highest artistry, rhetoric, and inimitability.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7/r1.anchor: في القرآن الكريم آيات وتعبيرات تتشابه مع تعبيرات أخرى ولا تختلف عنها إلا في مواطن ضئيلة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p812/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p812/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p812/r1.claim: The intellect calculates in a cool, measured way, while the heart moves a person to act on what they believe; logical reasoning alone may not produce such action.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p812/r1.anchor: العقل يأخذ الأمور بمحسوب رياضي والعقل منطقة باردة، أما القلب فهو الذي يحملك على العمل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p812/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p812/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p812/r2.claim: Quranic orthography and prosodic spelling each follow conventions that cannot be analogized; the Quran was written as the Companions wrote it, with forms such as نعمت/نعمة and رحمت/رحمة, and some spellings have no stated explanation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p812/r2.anchor: خطّان لا يُقاس عليهما خط المصحف وخط العَروض

NASHR:v2p247/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p247/r8.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
NASHR:v2p247/r8.claim: In four plural forms of أمهاتكم, Hamza kasrates hamza and mīm, while al-Kisai kasrates only hamza; both apply this in connected reading, unlike the other readers.
NASHR:v2p247/r8.anchor: بطون أمهاتكم، وفي النور أو بيوت أمهاتكم فكسر الهمزة والميم حمزة

QIRAAT-ER:16:78:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:16:78:6#1/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:16:78:6#1/r1.claim: One plural-stem pronunciation changes hamza from ḍamma to kasra and mīm from fatḥa to kasra, a dialectal vowel variant.
QIRAAT-ER:16:78:6#1/r1.anchor: Vowel shift: ḍamma to kasra on hamza (u→i), and fatha to kasra on mīm — dialectal variation

QIRAAT-ER:16:78:6#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:16:78:6#2/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:16:78:6#2/r1.claim: An intermediate form changes only hamza from ḍamma to kasra while mīm retains fatḥa.
QIRAAT-ER:16:78:6#2/r1.anchor: Vowel shift: ḍamma to kasra on hamza only (u→i), mīm retains fatḥa — intermediate variant

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r2.claim: After establishing the inevitable Hour and previously noting human ignorance, the passage recalls the first creation from mothers as evidence for the resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r2.anchor: ولما ذكر تعالى أمر الساعة وأنها كائنة لا محالة، فكان في ذلك دلالة على النشأة الآخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r3.claim: God's gift of the senses, means of perceiving and knowing, is a great blessing that calls for gratitude.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r3.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى امتنانه عليهم بجعل الحواس التي هي سبب لإدراك الأشياء والعلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r4.speaker: حمزة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r4.claim: Ḥamza reads the hamza and mīm of ummahātikum with kasra here and in al-Nūr, al-Zumar, and al-Najm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r4.anchor: وقرأ حمزة: بكسر الهمزة، والميم هنا وفي النور، والزمر، والنجم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r5.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r5.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads the hamza with kasra at these locations.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r6.speaker: الأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r6.claim: Al-Aʿmash omits the hamza and reads the mīm with kasra.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r7.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r7.claim: Ibn Abī Laylā omits the hamza and keeps the mīm fatḥa.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r7.anchor: وابن أبي ليلى بحذفها وفتح الميم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r8.speaker: أبو حاتم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r8.claim: Abū Ḥātim calls hamza deletion poor but judges Ibn Abī Laylā's reading sounder because kasra on mīm depends on the deleted hamza, unlike the preserved fatḥa.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r8.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: حذف الهمزة رديء، ولكن قراءة ابن أبي أصوب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r9.claim: Lā taʿlamūna is a circumstantial clause: you were knowing nothing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r9.anchor: ولا تعلمون جملة حالية أي: غير عالمين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r10.claim: Some say the newborns know nothing of the covenant taken from their fathers' loins, their decreed felicity or misery, or their interests; Abū Ḥayyān prefers the word's general scope, especially under negation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r10.anchor: وقالوا: لا تعلمون شيئا مما أخذ عليكم من الميثاق في أصلاب آبائكم، أو شيئا مما قضى عليكم من السعادة أو الشقاوة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r11.speaker: وهب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r11.claim: Wahb says a newborn remains ḥadhiran for seven days and perceives neither comfort nor pain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r11.anchor: وقال وهب: يولد المولود حذرا إلى سبعة أيام لا يدرك راحة ولا ألما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r12.claim: Wa-jaʿala may coordinate with akhrajakum within the same predicate, or begin an independent report coordinated with the opening clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r12.anchor: ويحتمل وجعل أن يكون معطوفا على أخرجكم، فيكون واحدا في حيز خبر المبتدأ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r13.claim: Hearing, sight, and hearts denote their faculties of sensation and perception, expressed through the names of the organs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r13.anchor: والمراد بالسمع والأبصار والأفئدة إحساسها وإدراكها، فعبر عن ذلك بالآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r14.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r14.claim: Al-Rāzī claims fuʾād is a paucity plural because hearts were created for certain knowledge, while most people pursue bestial acts; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this as foolish.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r14.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي ما معناه: إنما جمع الفؤاد جمع قلة، لأنه إنما خلق للمعارف الحقيقية اليقينية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r15.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls al-Rāzī's explanation nonsensical, saying he would not mention it but for the speaker's stature and its appearance in books.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p574/r15.anchor: وهو قول هذياني، ولولا جلالة قائله وتسطيره في الكتب ما ذكرته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p575/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p575/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p575/r3.claim: The three faculties are hearing, sight, and reason: the first two perceive sensible things and reason perceives intelligibles; the bird passage singles out sight as an unusually striking means of perceiving creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p575/r3.anchor: ولما ذكر تعالى مدارك العلم الثلاثة: السمع، والنظر، والعقل، والأولان مدرك المحسوس، والثالث مدرك المعقول

ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r1.claim: The clause coordinates with God’s making spouses from among people, joining both signs in the proof of divine oneness; al-Ālūsī finds this the more satisfying connection.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r1.anchor: عطف على قوله تعالى : ( والله جعل لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا ) منتظم معه في سلك أدلة التوحيد

ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r2.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r2.claim: Al-Ṭībī connects the clause with God’s power over everything; the conjunction signals that divine capacities are unlimited and the cited acts are only some of them.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r2.anchor: يفهم من قول العلامة الطيبي أنه تعالى عقب قوله سبحانه : ( إن الله على كل شيء قدير ) بقوله جل وعلا : ( والله أخرجكم )

ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r3.claim: The plural أمهات adds tāʾ to أم, commonly; the same meaning occurs without tāʾ, with the marked form used for humans and the unmarked form for animals.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r3.anchor: والأمهات بضم الهمزة وفتح الهمزة جمع أم والهاء فيه مزيدة وكثر زيادتها فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r4.claim: The singular’s pattern is supported by the Arabic verbal noun الأمومة; the form with tāʾ also occurs, though rarely.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r4.anchor: ووزن المفرد فعل لقولهم الأمومة وجاء بالهاء كقول قصي بن كلاب

ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r5.speaker: قصي بن كلاب
ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r5.claim: Qusayy ibn Kilāb’s poetic wording أمهتي is cited as evidence for the form with tāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p199#2/r5.anchor: كقول قصي بن كلاب عليهما الرحمة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r1.claim: Adding tāʾ to a verb, as in إهراق, is rarer still; al-Ālūsī refers readers to lexicons for the issue.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r1.anchor: وأقل من ذلك زيادة الهاء في الفعل كما قيل في إهراق وفيه بحث فارجع إلى الصحاح وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r2.claim: For this word and the locations named as al-Zumar, al-Najm, and al-Rum, Ḥamza reads both hamza and mīm with kasra; al-Kisāʾī reads mīm with kasra, al-Aʿmash drops hamza and kasras mīm, and Ibn Abī Laylā drops hamza and opens mīm.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة بكسر الهمزة والميم هنا وفي الزمر والنجم والروم والكسائي بكسر الميم فيهن

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r3.speaker: أبو حاتم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r3.claim: Abū Ḥātim calls dropping hamza poor but prefers Ibn Abī Laylā’s open mīm, since mīm’s kasra follows hamza and loses its basis when hamza is dropped.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r3.anchor: قال أبو حاتم : حذف الهمزة رديء ولكن قراءة ابن أبي ليلى أصوب وكانت كذلك على ما في البحر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r4.claim: لا تعلمون شيئا is circumstantial; شيئا can be a cognate accusative or an object, and the negation applies to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r4.anchor: في موضع الحال و ( شيئا ) منصوب على المصدرية أو مفعول ( تعلمون )

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r5.claim: Here knowledge means recognition: at birth people know nothing at all about their benefactor or anything else; the broader reading needs no narrowing.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r5.anchor: والعلم بمعنى المعرفة أي غير عارفين شيئا أصلا من حق المنعم وغيره وقيل : شيئا من منافعكم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r6.claim: Other proposed limits are that newborns know none of their interests, their foreordained happiness or misery, or the covenant taken in their fathers’ loins.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r6.anchor: وقيل : شيئا من منافعكم وقيل : مما قضى عليكم من السعادة أو الشقاوة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r7.speaker: وهب
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r7.claim: Wahb reports that newborns remain numb for seven days and perceive neither comfort nor pain.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r7.anchor: وعن وهب يولد المولود خدرا إلى سبعة أيام لا يدرك راحة ولا ألما

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r8.claim: Some philosophers argue that the soul is never wholly without knowledge at first, because it has immediate, presential awareness of itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r8.anchor: وادعى بعضهم أن النفس لا تخلو في مبدأ الفطرة عن العلم الحضوري وهو علمها بنفسها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r9.speaker: الشيخ
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r9.claim: The Shaykh argues that one is never unaware of oneself, even during sleep or intoxication; whoever allows such unawareness cannot use this proof of an immaterial soul.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r9.anchor: فقد قال الشيخ في بعض تعليقاته عند إثبات تجرد النفس : إنك لا تغفل عن ذاتك أصلا في حال من الأحوال

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r10.speaker: بهمنيار
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r10.claim: Bahmanyār says the soul senses itself, so its existence is intellectual and its existence is its perception; al-Shifāʾ gives a similar argument.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r10.anchor: وقال بهمنيار في التحصيل في فصل العقل والمعقول : ثم إن النفس الإنسانية تشعر بذاتها فيجب أن يكون وجودها عقليا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r11.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the no-absence proof relies on obscure, disputed premises, including the soul’s immateriality and the claim that every immaterial thing knows.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r11.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن عدم الخلو مبني على مقدمات خفية كتجرد النفس الذي أنكره الطبيعيون عن آخرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r12.claim: Self-identity need not itself be self-knowledge; otherwise everyone would know the immaterial soul’s essence, which is plainly not so, and awareness may require a condition.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r12.anchor: وأيضا إذا قلنا : إن حقيقة الذات غير غائبة عنها وقلنا : إن ذلك علم يلزم أن يكون حقيقة النفس المجردة معلومة لكل أحد

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r13.speaker: المحقق الطوسي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r13.claim: Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī denies that one is never unaware of oneself, citing loss of self-awareness during fainting and other mental illnesses.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r13.anchor: على أن المحقق الطوسي قد منع قولهم : إنك لا تغفل عن ذاتك أبدا وقال : إن المغمى عليه ربما غفل عن ذاته

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r14.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r14.claim: One scholar says initial blankness means the soul’s state before attachment to the body, so it does not conflict with a child’s instinctive attachment to the breast after birth.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r14.anchor: أن المراد بخلوها في مبدإ الفطرة خلوها حال تعلقها بالبدن وقال : إنه لا ينافي ذلك ما قاله الشيخ

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r15.claim: Al-Ālūsī calls that reconciliation strange: it places the blank state after attachment to the body and treats it as preceding the infant’s behavior.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r15.anchor: ووجه العجب ظاهر فافهم ولا تغفل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r16.speaker: العز
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r16.claim: Al-ʿIzz argues that knowledge cannot retain its ordinary sense with شيئا as a cognate object: that would require omitting two objects and would imply prior knowledge of the first.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r16.anchor: وفي أمالي العز لا يجوز أن يجعل باقيا على بابه ويكون ( شيئا ) مصدرا أي لا تعلمون علما لوجهين

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r17.claim: Al-Ālūsī answers that ordinary knowledge remains grammatical if شيئا is its first object and the second object is omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r17.anchor: ويعلم منه استقامة جعل العلم على بابه و ( شيئا ) مفعوله الأول والمفعول الثاني محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r18.claim: The clause about hearing, sight, and hearts may stand independently or coordinate with the preceding predicate; waw does not impose chronological order, and the faculties matter once active after birth.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r18.anchor: والواو لا تقتضي الترتيب ونكتة تأخيره

ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r19.claim: Jaʿala takes one object when it means create; when it means render, it takes two, with لكم as the second.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p200/r19.anchor: وجعل إن تعدى لواحد بأن كان بمعنى خلق فلكم متعلق به وإن تعدى لاثنين بأن كان بمعنى صير فهو مفعوله الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v14p201/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201/r1.claim: The senses supply particulars; repeated perception lets the heart distinguish similarities and differences, yielding immediate knowledge that can support acquired knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201/r1.anchor: والمعنى جعل لكم هذه الأشياء آلات تحصلون بها العلم والمعرفة بأن تحسوا بمشاعركم جزئيات الأشياء

ALUSI-FULL:v14p201/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201/r2.speaker: الحكماء
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201/r2.claim: Many philosophers say the soul begins without knowledge; the outer senses provide particular impressions through the imaginative faculty, preparing the Active Intellect to impart universals.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201/r2.anchor: ومستمد ما ذهب إليه الكثير من الحكماء من أن النفس في أول أمرها خالية عن العلوم فإذا استعملت الحواس الظاهرة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p201/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201/r3.speaker: الحكماء
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201/r3.claim: Philosophers distinguish four stages of intellect: potential, habitual, actual, and acquired.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201/r3.anchor: ويثبتوا للنفس أربع مراتب مرتبة العقل الهيولاني ومرتبة العقل بالملكة ومرتبة العقل بالفعل ومرتبة العقل المستفاد

ALUSI-FULL:v14p201/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201/r4.speaker: الحكماء
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201/r4.claim: The philosophers discussed here hold that the soul does not perceive material particulars; al-Ālūsī notes their lengthy debate.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201/r4.anchor: ويزعمون أن النفس لا تدرك الجزئي المادي ولهم في هذا المقام كلام طويل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r1.speaker: أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r1.claim: Sunnis hold that the soul apprehends universals and particulars, both through the senses and without them.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r1.anchor: وأهل السنة يقولون : إن النفس تدرك الكلي والجزئي مطلقا باستعمال المشاعر وبدونه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God gave these faculties so people hear His admonitions, see His blessings from birth to adulthood, and recognize His greatness.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما في هذه الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r3.claim: An alternative reading is that hearing receives Qurʾān and Sunna as transmitted proofs, sight examines wonders in creation, and hearts understand the meanings God made into signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r3.anchor: وقيل المعنى جعل لكم السمع لتسمعوا به نصوص الكتاب والسنة التي هي دلائل سمعية

ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r4.claim: On both explanations, hearing and sight retain their ordinary outward senses; al-Ālūsī knows of no commentator who takes them otherwise.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r4.anchor: والسمع والأبصار على هذين القولين على ظاهرهما ولم نر من جوز إخراجهما عن ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r5.claim: The first explanation takes the faculties as outward senses; أفئدة is the plural of فؤاد, the heart’s center as the heart is to the chest.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r5.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بهما الحواس الظاهرة على الأول والأفئدة جمع فؤاد وهو وسط القلب كالقلب من الصدر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says أفئدة is a plural-of-few form used like a plural-of-many because no other form is attested in usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r6.anchor: وهذا الجمع على ما في الكشاف من جموع القلة الجارية مجرى الكثرة والقلة إذ لم يرد في السماع غيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj says fuʾād has no regular plural of the greatest number, though أفئدة and فئدان occur, like أغربة and غربان for غراب.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r7.anchor: وقال الزجاج : لم يجمع فؤاد على أكثر العدد

ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r8.speaker: التفسير الكبير
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r8.claim: Al-Tafsīr al-Kabīr speculates that the few-form plural signals how rare true hearts are: most people pursue animal or predatory traits rather than certain knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r8.anchor: وفي التفسير الكبير لعل الفؤاد إنما جمع على بناء القلة تنبيها على أن السمع والبصر كثير

ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r9.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r9.claim: Al-Baḥr sharply criticizes that speculation and corrects the claim that شسوع is the sole plural of شسع, citing اشساع as another plural-of-few form.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r9.anchor: وفي البحر بعد نقله أنه قول مذياني ولولا جلالة قائله لم نسطره في الكتب

ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r10.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r10.claim: Some claim the heart perceives what is not bounded by spatial or quantitative categories, and that each object has a unique faculty of perception; al-Ālūsī dismisses this.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p201#2/r10.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن الفؤاد إنما يدرك ما ليس بمحدود بنو أين وكيف وكم وغير ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r1.claim: Hearing is singular because the word is originally a verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r1.anchor: وإفراد السمع باعتبار أنه مصدر في الأصل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r2.claim: One explanation is that hearing’s singular form reflects one kind of object perceived, while sight’s plural reflects its many kinds.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r2.anchor: وقيل : إنما أفرد وجمع الإبصار للإشارة إلى أن مدركاته نوع واحد ومدركات البصر أكثر من ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r3.claim: Other explanations for placing hearing first are that it receives revelation or that hearing develops before sight; another says auditory objects are fewer.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r3.anchor: وتقديمه لما أنه طريق تلقي الوحي أو لأن إدراكه أقدم من إدراك البصر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r4.claim: Hearing and sight precede the heart because outward perception comes before inward perception, or because they serve and contribute to the heart’s cognition.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r4.anchor: وتقديمها على الأفئدة المشار بها إلى العقل لتقدم الظاهر على الباطن أو لأن لهما مدخلا في إدراكه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r5.claim: A further comparison says servants precede masters, and outward senses have fewer objects than the heart’s nearly innumerable objects, though both intellect and sight have limits.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r5.anchor: بل هما من خدمه والخدم تتقدم بين يدي السادة وكثير من السنن أمر بتقديمه على فروض العبادة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r6.claim: Some take mention of hearing and sight alone as evidence against the five inward senses proposed by philosophers; al-Ālūsī says the issue needs fuller discussion.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r6.anchor: واستأنس بعضهم بذكر ما يشير إليه فقط دون ضم ما يشير إلى سائر المشاعر الباطنية إليه لنفي الحواس الخمس الباطنة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r7.claim: One explanation is that people recognize God’s successive favors and therefore thank Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r7.anchor: كي تعرفوا ما أنعم سبحانه عليكم طورا غب طور فتشكروه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r8.claim: Another explanation is that God gave these faculties so people would thank Him by using them for their intended purposes.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p202/r8.anchor: وقيل : المعنى جعل ذلك كي تشكروه تعالى باستعمال ما ذكر فيما خلق لأجله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r3.speaker: الكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r3.claim: Al-Kisa'i reads the hamza of ummahāt with kasra.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r4.speaker: حمزة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r4.claim: Hamza reads both the mīm and hamza with kasra.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r4.anchor: وقرأ حمزة بكسر الميم والهمزة، الباقون بضم الهمزة وفتح الميم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r5.speaker: الباقون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r5.claim: The other readers use a ḍamma on the hamza and fatḥa on the mīm.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r6.claim: The statement that they knew nothing completes a sentence; a new one begins with God giving them hearing, sight, and hearts, which He created before birth, while knowledge came after birth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r6.anchor: {لا تعلمون شيئا} تم الكلام، ثم ابتدأ فقال جل وعلا {وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p34/r7.claim: These gifts are given so that people may give thanks for God's blessing.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r6.claim: God's power over everything includes raising creatures at once, as He demonstrated by bringing them into existence gradually from their mothers' wombs.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r6.anchor: فيقدر أن يحيي الخلائق دفعة كما قدر أن أحياهم متدرجا

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r7.speaker: الكسائي وحمزة
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r7.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads the hamza of أمهات with kasra as a dialect or by assimilation; Ḥamza reads its hamza, mīm, and hāʾ with kasra, adding a hāʾ like أهراق.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r7.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي بكسر الهمزة على أنه لغة أو إتباع لما قبلها

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r8.claim: Newborns know nothing and begin in a state of ignorance likened to lifeless matter.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r9.claim: Hearing, sight, and hearts let people sense particulars, recognize likenesses and differences through repeated perception, gain self-evident knowledge, and acquire further knowledge by reasoning.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r9.anchor: أداة تتعلمون بها فتحسون بمشاعركم جزئيات الأشياء فتدركونها

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r10.claim: These faculties are given so people recognize God's successive favors and give thanks.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:77-78/r10.anchor: كي تعرفوا ما أنعم عليكم طورا بعد طور فتشكروه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r5.claim: After rebuking their false belief and ending with the Hour, the discourse turns to first creation as evidence of the Hour and of God’s power to act by choice.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r5.anchor: ولما انتقضى توبيخهم على إيمانهم بالباطل وكفرانهم بالحق

BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r6.claim: God brought people from their mothers’ wombs knowing nothing, great or small; the One who did this can bring them from the earth even more readily.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r6.anchor: والذي أخرجكم منها قادر على إخراجكم من بطن الأرض بلا فرق بل بطريق الأولى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r7.claim: Hearing, sight, and hearts are faculties for removing the ignorance present at birth; God formed them in the inaccessible womb, so recreating people is easier still.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r7.anchor: آلات لإزالة الجهل الذي وقعت الولادة عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r8.claim: Biqāʿī suggests hearing is singular while sight and hearts are plural because variation in them is greater, though only God knows its full extent.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r8.anchor: لأن التفاوت فيهما أكثر من التفاوا فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r9.claim: The afʾida are hearts prepared to understand and regulate the body through the subtle heat within them, which can receive delicate meanings.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r9.anchor: والأفئدة هي القلوب التي هيأها للفهم وإصلاح البدن بما أودعها من الحرارة اللطيفة القابلة للمعاني الدقيقة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r10.claim: The faculties may bring people to gratitude when they hear admonitions and see signs, recognize God’s knowledge, power, and care, and acknowledge what His messengers conveyed.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r10.anchor: بمعارف القلوب التي وهبكموها إذا سمعتم المواعظ وأبصرتم الآيات

BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r11.claim: The chief lesson is that the benefactor is one God, all-knowing, all-powerful, and freely acting; natural forces are created and act only as He directs them.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p295/r11.anchor: المنعم عليكم بهذه النعم إله واحد عالم بكل شيء

DURR-FULL:v5p152/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p152/r7.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p152/r7.claim: Al-Suddī explains the mothers’ bellies as the womb.
DURR-FULL:v5p152/r7.anchor: عن السدي في قوله: {والله أخرجكم من بطون أمهاتكم} قال: من الرحم

DURR-FULL:v5p152/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p152/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p152/r8.claim: Qatāda calls hearing, sight, and hearts an honor God bestowed on people and urges them to thank Him for the gift.
DURR-FULL:v5p152/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة لعلكم تشكرون} قال: كرامة أكرمكم الله بها فاشكروا نعمه

DURR-FULL:v5p152/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p152/r9.speaker: حبة وسواء ابنا خالد
DURR-FULL:v5p152/r9.claim: Hubba and Sawāʾ ibn Khālid report the Prophet’s assurance not to despair of provision: every child is born bare, then God provides for them.
DURR-FULL:v5p152/r9.anchor: عن حبة وسواء ابني خالد أنهما أتيا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: وهو يعالج بناء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r8.claim: God counts a clear blessing: He brought people out ignorant, then made their bestowed senses a ladder for acquiring knowledge so they would thank Him and believe.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r8.anchor: آية تعديد نعمة بينة لا ينكرها عاقل، وهي نعمة معها كفرها وتصريفها في الإشراك بالذي وهبها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r9.claim: Abu Ishaq says أمهات derives from أمات with an added hāʾ for emphasis, as in أهرقت الماء.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r9.anchor: أصله أمات، وزيدت الهاء مبالغة وتأكيدا، كما زادوا الهاء في أهرقت الماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r10.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r10.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read إمهاتكم with kasra on the initial hamza.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r11.speaker: الأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r11.claim: Al-Aʿmash omits the hamza and gives the doubled mīm a kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r11.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش «في بطون امهاتكم» بحذف الهمزة وكسر الميم المشددة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r12.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى وأبو حاتم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r12.claim: Ibn Abi Layla omits the hamza and gives the doubled mīm a fatḥa; Abu Hatim calls omission bad but considers this reading sounder.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r12.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي ليلى بحذف الهمزة وفتح الميم مشددة، قال أبو حاتم: حذف الهمزة ردي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p411/r13.claim: The expectation expressed by لعل is from the human audience's perspective.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r1.claim: Hamza reads imhātikum with kasra on both initial alif and mīm; al-Kisaʾi has kasra on the alif and fatḥa on the mīm; the rest read with fatḥa on the mīm and ḍamma on the alif.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة إمهاتكم بكسر الألف والميم وقرأ الكسائي بكسر الإلف وفتح الميم والباقون بضم الألف وفتح الميم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r2.claim: The same readings occur at 24:61, 39:6, and 53:32, with no disagreement among readers on the form when beginning recitation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r2.anchor: وكذلك في ( النور 61 ) و ( الزمر 6 ) و ( النجم 32 ) ولا خلاف بينهم في الابتداء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r3.claim: Al-samʿ is grammatically singular in form but refers to hearing collectively; the author points back to 2:7.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r3.anchor: ﴿ وجعل لكم السمع ﴾ لفظه لفظ الواحد والمراد به الجميع وقد بينا علة ذلك في أول ( البقرة 7 )

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says afʾida is the plural of fuʾād, like ghurāb/aghreba, and it has no larger plural fuʾdān analogous to ghurbān.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r4.anchor: والأفئدة جمع فؤاد قال الزجاج مثل غراب وأغربة ولم يجمع فؤاد على أكثر العدد لم يقل فيه فئدان مثل غراب وغربان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r5.claim: Abu ʿUbayda says these faculties were created before birth, though the verse mentions them afterward, since Arabic can reverse the order of a list.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r5.anchor: وإنما جعل لهم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة قبل أن يخرجهم غير أن العرب تقدم وتؤخر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r6.claim: The cited line says al-shanaq is between two assessed dues and al-muʾūn is larger, so it names the lesser before the greater.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r6.anchor: ضخم تعلق أشناق الديات به إذا المؤون أمرت فوقه حملا الشنق ما بين الفريضتين والمؤون أعظم من الشنق فبدأ بالأقل قبل الأعظم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r7.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r7.claim: The verse displays God's favor: He brings people out ignorant and gives them faculties by which they acquire knowledge.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p475/r7.anchor: قال المفسرون ومقصود الآية أن الله تعالى أبان نعمه عليهم حيث أخرجهم جهالا بالأشياء وخلق لهم الآلات التي يتوصلون بها إلى العلم

JISHUMI:v6p4080/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4080/r4.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v6p4080/r4.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read إمهاتكم with kasra on the initial hamza; the other readers use damma.
JISHUMI:v6p4080/r4.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: إمهاتكم بكسر الهمزة، والباقون بضمها

JISHUMI:v6p4080/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4080/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4080/r11.claim: Hearing is singular while sight is plural throughout much of the Quran because hearing is a verbal noun and sight names the eyes.
JISHUMI:v6p4080/r11.anchor: جمع (الأبصار) ووحد (السمع) وكذلك هو في أكثر المواضع من القرآن، لأن السمع مصدر سمع

JISHUMI:v6p4080/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4080/r12.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4080/r12.claim: Alternatively, singular al-samʿ is a generic collective noun.

JISHUMI:v6p4080/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4080/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4080/r13.claim: Ummahāt originally was umāt; the added hāʾ emphasizes the word, as in ahraqt from araqt.
JISHUMI:v6p4080/r13.anchor: أمهاتكم أصله: أماتكم، زيدت الهاء للتأكيد كأهرقت وأصله أرقت

MUQATIL:16:77-78/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:77-78/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:77-78/r4.claim: People are born knowing nothing, and God subsequently teaches them.
MUQATIL:16:77-78/r4.anchor: لا تعلمون شيئا } ، فعلمكم بعد ذلك الجهل

MUQATIL:16:77-78/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:77-78/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:77-78/r5.claim: The hearts are what is meant by the faculties called afʾida.

MUQATIL:16:77-78/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:77-78/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:77-78/r6.claim: They should thank the Lord for these blessings of fine creation by affirming His oneness.
MUQATIL:16:77-78/r6.anchor: رب هذه النعم تعالى ذكره في حسن خلقكم فتوحدونه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r1.claim: The following verse is evidence of God's power.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r1.anchor: ثم دل على قدرته بما بعده فقال

NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r2.claim: Some read the alif with kasra and mīm with fatḥa following the preceding nūn; Ḥamza reads both with kasra.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r2.anchor: وبكسر الألف وفتح الميم على اتباعا لكسرة النون وبكسرهما حمزة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r3.claim: The hāʾ in ummahāt is emphatic, as in ahraqa from arāqa; its addition in the singular is anomalous.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r3.anchor: والهاء مزيدة في امهات للتوكيد كما زيدت في أراف فقيل أهراق وشذت زيادتها في الواحدة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r4.claim: This clause is circumstantial: the newborn knew nothing of the Benefactor's rights.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r4.anchor: حال أي غير عالمين شيئا من حق المنعم الذي خلقكم في البطون

NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r5.claim: These faculties remove birth's ignorance and acquire knowledge and action: gratitude, worship, and fulfilling God's rights.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r5.anchor: إلا آلات لإزالة الجهل الذي ولدتم عليه واجتلاب العلم والعمل به من شكر المنعم وعبادته والقيام بحقوقه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r6.claim: Afʾida is plural of fuʾād like aghriba from gharīb; this plural of paucity serves abundance because no other form is attested.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p265#2/r6.anchor: والأفئدة في فؤاد كالأغربة في غراب وهو من جموع القلة التي جرت مجرى جموع الكثرة لعدم السماع في غيرها

QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r1.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r1.claim: One interpretation is that people initially knew nothing of the covenant taken from them in their fathers' loins.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r1.anchor: وفيه ثلاثة أقاويل: أحدها لا تعلمون شيئا مما أخذ عليكم من الميثاق في أصلاب آبائكم.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r2.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r2.claim: A second interpretation is that people knew nothing of the happiness or misery decreed for them.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r2.anchor: الثاني لا تعلمون شيئا مما قضى عليكم من السعادة والشقاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r3.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r3.claim: A third interpretation is that people knew none of their benefits.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r3.anchor: الثالث لا تعلمون شيئا من منافعكم وتم الكلام، ثم ابتدأ فقال:

QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r4.claim: The clause about knowing nothing ends at شيئا; وجعل لكم begins a new clause.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r4.anchor: وتم الكلام، ثم ابتدأ فقال: { وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة }

QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r5.claim: Hearing, sight, and hearts are faculties for learning and perception; though created earlier, God granted them after birth.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r5.anchor: أي التي تعلمون بها وتدركون لأن الله جعل ذلك لعباده قبل إخراجهم من البطون

QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r6.claim: Hearing receives commands and prohibitions, sight sees traces of God's workmanship, and hearts lead to knowledge of Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r6.anchor: السمع لتسمعوا به الأمر والنهي، والأبصار لتبصروا بها آثار صنعه، والأفئدة لتصلوا بها إلى معرفته.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r7.claim: Afʾida is the plural of fuʾād, like غراب and أغربة.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r7.anchor: والأفئدة: جمع الفؤاد نحو غراب وأغربة.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r8.claim: One view infers speech from hearing: the deaf do not speak, and the presence of hearing entails speech.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r8.anchor: وقد قيل في ضمن قوله «وجعل لكم السمع» إثبات النطق لأن من لم يسمع لم يتكلم

QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r9.speaker: الأعمش وابن وثاب وحمزة
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r9.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Ibn Waththāb, and Ḥamza read إمهاتكم with kasra on hamza and mīm here and in the named sūras.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r9.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وابن وثاب وحمزة «إمهاتكم» هنا وفي النور والزمر والنجم، بكسر الهمزة والميم.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r10.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r10.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads with kasra on hamza and fatḥa on mīm, by vowel assimilation.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r10.anchor: وأما الكسائي فكسر الهمزة وفتح الميم وإنما كان هذا للإتباع

QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r11.speaker: الباقون
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r11.claim: The other readers retain the original ḍamma on hamza and fatḥa on mīm.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r11.anchor: الباقون بضم الهمزة وفتح الميم على الأصل

QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r12.claim: The original form was أمات; hāʾ was added for emphasis, as in أهرقت from أرقت.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r12.anchor: وأصل الأمهات: أمات، فزيدت الهاء تأكيدا كما زادوا هاء في أهرقت الماء وأصله أرقت.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r13.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r13.claim: One explanation is that the faculties enable people to thank God for His blessings.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r14.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r14.claim: Another explanation is that people see signs of God's workmanship, whose perception leads to gratitude.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:78/r14.anchor: الثاني يعني تبصرون آثار صنعته لأن إبصارها يؤدي إلى الشكر.

BURSEVI:v5p48/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p48/r1.claim: Ummahāt is the plural of umm (mother), with an added hāʾ, as in ihraq from araq.
BURSEVI:v5p48/r1.anchor: جمع الأم زيدت الهاء فيها كما زيدت في الإهراق من أراق

BURSEVI:v5p48/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p48/r2.claim: At birth people know nothing of worldly or afterlife matters, including what their souls knew in the spirit world, what their atoms knew at the primordial covenant, or the innate skills animals display when seeking their mothers and food.
BURSEVI:v5p48/r2.anchor: أي : حال كونكم غير عالمين شيئا أصلا من أمور الدنيا والآخرة

BURSEVI:v5p48/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48/r3.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
BURSEVI:v5p48/r3.claim: Saʿdi's couplet contrasts an ant that emerges from its egg and seeks food with a human born without awareness, reason, or discernment.
BURSEVI:v5p48/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ سعدي قدس سره : مر غك از بيضه برون

BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r1.claim: Hearing is mentioned before sight because it receives revelation and because some prophets lost sight but not hearing; alternatively, hearing develops before sight, as a newborn's eyes open later.
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r1.anchor: قدمه على البصر لما أنه طريق تلقى الوحي ولذا ابتلي بعض الأنبياء بالعمى دون الصمم أو لأن إدراكه أقدم

BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r2.claim: Samʿ is singular because it was originally a verbal noun.
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r2.anchor: وإفراده باعتبار كونه مصدرا في الأصل

BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r3.claim: Absār is the plural of baṣar, the sense of the eye.
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r3.anchor: جمع بصر وهي محركة حس العين

BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r4.claim: Afʾidah is the plural of fuʾād, the heart's center; it relates to the heart as the heart relates to the chest.
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r4.anchor: جمع فؤاد وهو وسط القلب وهو من القلب كالقلب من الصدر

BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r5.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r5.claim: Although afʾidah is a small-number plural, it serves for abundance here and in similar verses because the address “for you” is general.
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r5.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" : استعملت في هذه الآية

BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r6.claim: These faculties are instruments for knowledge: the senses register particulars, and the heart notices similarities and differences through repeated sensations, enabling new and acquired knowledge.
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r6.anchor: جعل لكم هذه الأشياء آلات تحصلون بها العلم والمعرفة بأن تحسوا بمشاعركم جزئيات الأشياء

BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r7.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r7.claim: The conjunction with “He brought you out” joins the events without fixing their order; the faculties' effects appear only after birth, though they already existed potentially.
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r7.anchor: وليس فيه دلالة على تأخر الجعل المذكور عند الإخراج لما أن مدلول الواو هو الجمع مطلقا

BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r8.claim: He arranges seven divine attributes—life, knowledge, will, power, hearing, sight, and speech—and relates the sequence of human development from hearing through sight to speech to this pattern of perfection.
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r8.anchor: تعالى صفات سبعا مرتبة وهي الحياة والعلم والإرادة والقدرة والسمع والبصر والكلام

BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r9.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r9.claim: A prophetic report forbids a believer from impregnating another man's already occupied field; Bursevī invokes it in discussing a pregnant woman's marriage.
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r9.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر لا يسقين

BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r10.claim: Marriage to a pregnant woman is forbidden when pregnancy comes from a lawful marriage; the ruling for pregnancy from illicit sex is disputed.
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r10.anchor: ولذا حرم تزوج الحبلى من النكاح اتفاقا ومن الزنى اختلافا

BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r11.claim: A report says a fetus's hearing and sight become sharper through intercourse, supporting the discussion of prenatal faculties.
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r11.anchor: قلنا قد جاء في الخبر "إن سمع الحمل وبصره يزداد حده بالوطىء"

BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r12.claim: Gratitude means using hearing for God's speech, the Prophet's reports, and the wisdom of saints, and using sight to read God's signs and infer His existence, unity, knowledge, and power; misuse betrays His trusts.
BURSEVI:v5p48#2/r12.anchor: وشكرها استعمالها فيما خلقت لأجله من استماع كلام الله وأحاديث رسول الله وحكم أوليائه

BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r1.speaker: الشيخ السعدي
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r1.claim: Saʿdi's verses urge careful listening to the Qur'an and avoiding falsehood, and praise attending to the Creator's artistry while overlooking a brother's faults.
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r1.anchor: كذر كاه قرآن وندس كوش به بهتان وباطل شنيدن مكوش

BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r2.speaker: صائب
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r2.claim: The cited couplet calls the heart a trustee and warns against sleeping while God's trust is exposed to thieves.
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r2.anchor: وقال الصائب : ترابكو هردل كرده اند امانتدار

BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r3.claim: At the bodily level humans receive senses like animals; their spirits receive hearing, sight, and understanding like angels; their innermost secrets hear, see, and know through God.
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r3.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {وجعل لكم السمع والابصار والافادة}

BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r4.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r4.claim: The cited sacred report says God becomes the servant's hearing, sight, and tongue, through which the servant hears, sees, and speaks.
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r4.anchor: كنت له سمعا وبصرا ولسانا فبي يسمع وبي يبصر وبي ينطق

BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r5.claim: Gratitude for these faculties means using them to seek God, looking past the gifts to the Giver.
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r5.anchor: وأداء شكر نعم الله باستعمالها وصرفها في طلب الله وترك الالتفات إلى النعم بل للمنعم

BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r6.claim: The mothers' wombs signify nonexistence, the true mother; before God taught all names, people knew nothing.
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r6.anchor: أي : من العدم وهو الأم الحقيقي لا تعلمون شيئا قبل أن يعلمكم الله أسماء كل شيء

BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r7.claim: At the primordial address “Am I not your Lord?”, God's disclosure of lordship gave them a tongue, through the light of His hearing, to answer “Yes.”
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r7.anchor: حين خاطبكم بقوله : ألست بربكم فتجلى لكم بروبوبيته فبنور سمعه أعطاكم لسانا

BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r8.claim: The inward gratitude is to hear only God's speech, see only His beauty, love only His essence, and speak only with Him.
BURSEVI:v5p48#3/r8.anchor: فلا تسمعون بهذا السمع إلا كلامه ولا تبصرون بهذا البصر إلا جماله

RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r2.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read إمهاتكم with kasra on the hamza; the other readers use ḍamma.
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r2.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي ' إمهاتكم ' بكسر الهمزة ، والباقون بضمها

RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r3.claim: أمهات derives from أمات by adding hāʾ, as in أراق/أهراق; its addition in the singular is rare, as the cited verse line shows.
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r3.anchor: أمهاتكم أصله أماتكم ، إلا أنه زيد الهاء فيه كما زيد في أراق فقيل : أهراق وشذت زيادتها في الواحدة

RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r4.claim: Human beings begin life’s innate state empty of knowledge of things.
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r4.anchor: الإنسان خلق في مبدأ الفطرة خاليا عن معرفة الأشياء

RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r5.claim: Knowledge is either acquired or self-evident; acquired concepts and judgments depend on prior self-evident knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r5.anchor: التصورات والتصديقات إما أن تكون كسبية ، وإما أن تكون بديهية ، والكسبيات إنما يمكن تحصيلها بواسطة تركيبات البديهيات

RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r6.claim: Rāzī poses a regress problem: axioms cannot have been present before birth, yet if acquired they would require earlier knowledge without end.
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r6.anchor: هذه العلوم البديهية إما أن يقال أنها كانت حاصلة منذ خلقنا أو ما كانت حاصلة

RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r7.claim: He answers that these self-evident truths were initially absent from our minds and arose later.
RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r7.anchor: الحق أن هذه العلوم البديهية ما كانت حاصلة في نفوسنا ، ثم إنها حدثت وحصلت

RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r1.claim: Rāzī rejects the claim that newly arising axioms must be acquired: the senses can cause them to arise without prior learning.
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r1.anchor: هذه المقدمة ممنوعة ، بل نقول : إنها إنما حدثت في نفوسنا بعد عدمها بواسطة إعانة الحواس

RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r2.claim: Repeated seeing and hearing imprint the sensed things’ forms in imagination; the other senses similarly supply particulars for the mind.
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r2.anchor: فإذا أبصر الطفل شيئا مرة بعد أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r3.claim: When certain conceptions are present, they suffice for necessary judgments; theoretical conclusions instead need a separate proof and prior knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r3.anchor: ما يكون نفس حضوره موجبا تاما في جزم الذهن بإسناد بعضها إلى بعض بالنفي أو الإثبات

RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r4.claim: The senses supply conceptions, conceptions occasion axioms, and axioms enable acquired knowledge; God’s gift of the senses is therefore the first cause of knowledge in minds.
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r4.anchor: فظهر أن السبب الأول لحدوث هذه المعارف في النفوس والعقول هو أنه تعالى أعطى هذه الحواس

RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r5.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r5.claim: The commentators explain hearing as receiving God’s admonitions, sight as seeing His proofs, and hearts as grasping His greatness.
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r5.anchor: لتبصروا دلائل الله ، والأفئدة لتعقلوا عظمة الله

RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r6.claim: أفئدة is the plural of فؤاد, on the pattern of أغربة from غراب.
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r6.anchor: والأفئدة جمع فؤاد نحو أغربة وغراب

RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r7.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj says فؤاد has no larger-count plural; the passage also mentions فئدان by analogy with غراب/غران.
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r7.anchor: قال لازجاج : ولم يجمع فؤاد على أكثر العدد

RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r8.claim: Rāzī suggests the small-number plural signals that true hearts are few: most people are absorbed in animal appetites and predatory traits.
RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r8.anchor: لعل الفؤاد إنما جمع على بناء جمع القلة تنبيها على أن السمع والبصر كثيران وأن الفؤاد قليل

RAZI-FULL:v20p73/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p73/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p73/r1.claim: The conjunction does not require temporal order; alternatively, hearing and sight can mean listening and seeing, removing the chronological objection.
RAZI-FULL:v20p73/r1.anchor: حرف الواو لا يوجب الترتيب ؛ وأيضا إذا حملنا السمع على الاستماع والأبصار على الرؤية زال السؤال
